figures.caption: Figure 3. True and DCMA estimated interventional outcome distributions. Panels (A)–(C) show the true (black) and DCMA–ES estimated (red) densities for Y0M0 , Y1M0 , and Y1M1 , respectively. The DCMA estimate is obtained by pointwise averaging over 100 replications, and the shaded region denotes the 95% inter-replication interval defined by the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles across replications.

Figure 4. Quantile-based mediation effect estimates. Panels (A) and (B) correspond to Scenarios S1 and S2, respectively. Solid lines denote the true quantile effects, dashed lines denote the DCMA estimates, and shaded regions denote the 95% interreplication interval, defined by the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles across Monte Carlo replications.

Figure 5. Distributions and normality diagnostics of BMI, total cholesterol, and systolic blood pressure. The upper panels display histograms (gray bars) overlaid with kernel density estimates (solid lines) and fitted normal curves (dashed lines), while the lower panels present the corresponding Q–Q plots against the theoretical normal distribution.
